niche.title: 8 Cranial Bones Mnemonic: Old People From Texas Eat Spiders | Skull Anatomy #shorts
niche.description:
Can you name all 8 cranial bones? One silly sentence does it: Old People From Texas Eat Spiders 🦴

O → Occipital: the back of your skull (the spinal cord exits through its foramen magnum)
P → Parietal: top and sides (a pair)
F → Frontal: your forehead
T → Temporal: right above your ears (a pair)
E → Ethmoid: tucked between your eye sockets
S → Sphenoid: the "keystone" that joins almost every other skull bone
6 names, but parietal and temporal come in pairs = 8 cranial bones.

Quick test: your spinal cord leaves the skull through which bone? Answer in the video.

niche.title: 6 Deep Hip Rotators Mnemonic: P-GO-GO-Q (Piriformis to Quadratus Femoris) #shorts
niche.description:
Can you name all 6 deep hip rotators? One word does it, top to bottom: P-GO-GO-Q 🍑

P → Piriformis (the top one, from the sacrum)
G → Gemellus superior
O → Obturator internus (its tendon runs between the two gemelli, "little twins")
G → Gemellus inferior
O → Obturator externus (hidden deep, behind quadratus femoris)
Q → Quadratus femoris (the bottom one)
All 6 run to the greater trochanter area of the femur and rotate the thigh outward (lateral rotation).

Quick test: which big nerve exits just below piriformis? Answer in the video.

Save this for your next anatomy exam.

niche.title: Pancreas #anatomy
How a Cut Heals 😮
niche.description:
When you cut yourself, tiny blood vessels in your skin break open. Platelets plug the broken ends, fibrin threads trap red cells into a clot, and the clot's top dries into a scab. White blood cells squeeze out of nearby vessels to eat germs that got in. New tissue fills the gap from below, skin cells slide in under the scab, and when the scab falls off, the new tissue stays as a scar.

This is an animation, not microscopy: the cells are drawn far bigger than life, days and weeks are sped up into seconds, and in a real wound these steps overlap. Many scars fade over months.

Sources: MedlinePlu

niche.title: Broken Bones Heal Without a Scar, Unlike Most Tissues #science #howthebodyworks #anatomy
niche.description:
A twisting ski fall snaps a shin bone, and we dive inside to watch it rebuild: a blood clot bridges the gap, soft cartilage steadies the break, then it hardens into new bone. Over the following months the extra lump is carved away until the bone is back to its old shape.

Bone is one of the few tissues that heals without a scar: after months of remodelling, the break often leaves no outside trace and the bone is often just as strong as before.

Sources:
- Marsell R, Einhorn TA (2011). The biology of fracture healing. Injury 42(6):551-555 (PMC) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3105171/
